# Chapter Twelve: Check and Mate (Part III)

Check and Mate

sat behind the table in the small shack that he called home, before him were lists of supplies and other items the camp needed in order to survive but he wasn’t concentrating on thise. Instead his mind wandered, the armies of the Empress were coming North, they would roll over the camps killing everyone in them. He had made a vow to protect these people he thought. Nero swept his hand over the desk scattering the papers across the floor the impudent rage overwhelming him.

“Messenger?” Came the concerned voice of Gilread from the door. Nero sighed “Im okay my friend, just frustrated, please come in” he said motioning the other man to enter. “I understand, but Messenger what can we do?” he asked, and Nero knew the question was rhetorical and didn’t bother to answer. He needed to move his people; they couldn’t stay here, not with the army coming. But if he was going to move the refugees, he would need an escort and a place to go, somewhere out of the line of the oncoming invasion. He was the now the Lord Reagent of Vicor, he had the power to request aid he thought and just as hope began to spring up, it was smashed into the ground, crushed under the boot of reality.

In order to send a request to the other Lord Reagents he would need the seal otherwise the message would not be accepted and that had been left in the keep, he had been right there, he should have grabbed it, should have thought ahead he chastised himself for his own careless stupidity.

Something nagged at him, something about the seal he just couldn’t place his finger on it “Sir?” Gilread gently asked and Nero waived him off, trying to follow the line of thought that was trying to get his attention. “The seal” he whispered, “What about the seal” and then like a boulder it hit him, of course he thought how he had not thought of that sooner. “Gilread, I need to travel it’s only a two-day round trip and its imperative we make it” he breathed, and the other man looked startled. “Messenger, what could possibly be more important then protecting the camp?” he asked and Nero looked into his eyes and could see the question, was Nero going to abandon them, leave them to deal with the soldiers while he spirited himself off to safety and his heart Fell.

“We need to move the refugees, but in order to do that we need an escort and protection, but I doubt the Silvan’s will free up the men to do that. I am now the Lord Reagent and can request a contingent of Aurtus’s guard from the other Lord Reagents, but in order to do that I need the Seal of Aurtus” he said and Gilread looked at him confused and Nero sighed.

“Every Lord Reagent is buried with there seal” he began. “There is one buried half a day from here, if I can retrieve the seal, I can send a message and we can move these people out of harms way” he finished and Gilread slowly nodded, working through the logic himself and then it hit him. “Of course, Messenger, I will get it setup, when do you wish to leave?” he asked, and Nero smiled up at him. “Now if we can” he answered knowing the clock was ticking and they did not have the luxury of time.

Two hours later Gilread send someone to retrieve Nero when he arrived, he was shocked to find two horses packed with supplies and ready to go. “How did you manage that; the guards didn’t protest?” he asked amazed and the other man smiled. “When I told them we were leaving the Northern Territory they couldn’t get them together fast enough, apparently we are a bit of a political problem, the less that are here, the easier it is to sweep it under the carpet Messenger, though I did not manage to tell them we would be returning” he finished and grinned sheepishly “He scrambled to ensure everything was ready, I could barely keep him still long enough to explain to me what you were doing” called a familiar voice as Meric came around the horse a pack half hanging from his back, he handed it to Gilread giving his mate a gentle kiss and turned to the Messenger, the fierce looked in the otherwise unassuming man took him back a moment “Bring him back to me Messenger, keep him safe” Meric said grabbing and squeezing Gilread’s hand but his eyes never leaving Nero’s. The Messenger understood and nodded “On my life Meric, I will bring him back safe” he said, the other man searched the Messengers eyes for a moment and then nodded accepting the vow, he turned and with one last kiss left the two standing there. Nero mounted the horse and waited until Gilread did the same. “I wasn’t going to let you go alone, you might need help” he said, and Nero nodded. Remembering the look Meric had given him he knew he would bring this man back alive; he had vowed it. “Stay with me and if I tell you to run, you run” he simply said but knowing Gilread would never leave the Messenger, never abandon him, it wasn’t in him to do so.

The two of them rode out of the camp and urged the horses on as they rode towards the south, trying to fight the clock. They rode keeping an eye our for soldiers but the ride to the outskirts of the small village was uneventful. “Messenger” Gilread called as they began to see the remains of farms passing by turning, he saw the confused look on the man’s face. “What is it Gilread, you look troubled” he said He gathered his thoughts, looking to the remains of a farm as they passed, the house having not seen maintenance in what looked like a year as the roof slumped inward and the pen’s abandoned. “I understood that all Lord Reagents were buried within the tomb of the Knights in Aurtus’s keep, how is it there is one who is not?” he asked but there was no suspicion in his voice, only curiousity. Nero smiled remembering when he had heard the story.

“Lord Reagent Kolprise, was a bit of a womanizer in his time, despite the oaths he took, before his death he was disgraced and secretly stepped down as Lord Reagent, his proctor instead leading the church until his death. But since he was officially a Lord Reagent upon his death, he was buried in his robes of office with all of the traditional items. But because of his disgrace he was refused burial within the tomb, instead being buried in his childhood home” Nero said and Gilread nodded.

They continued to ride but as dusk began to settle over the land, they spotted there first problem. Riding over the hill the mostly fallen wall that surrounded the village came into view and the stopped, crouching down as they spied the small guard contingent that patrolled around the old Village. “What are they doing here?” Gilread hissed eyeing the four soldiers on horseback. Nero shook his head, trying to get a better look at them “I don’t know I figured they would all be preparing for the invasion, the Empress cannot have enough soldiers for a detail to be wasted on an abandoned village” he answered. The two men moved their horses into a barn of the farm that sat closest to the village. Most of the old roof was missing and it hadn’t seen an animal in a long time, but the walls were still sturdy, and they would be hidden from sight of the patrol. “What are they doing here?” Gilread whispered his eyes lighted by the small slit of light he was using to spy the location of the patrol. Nero shook his head and frustration, they needed to get into that village, needed to get into the keep and at every turn the Empress seemed to have roadblocks up, granted they were most likely not here for them, but that didn’t matter, if the soldiers found them,they will be killed or shipped over to the nearest village as slaves.

“We will wait until dark, then try to enter the village, we need to get to the keep Gilread, we have come too far and we need to get in there desperately if we are to help our people” Nero said shoring up his own resolve as he tried to bolster Gilreads. The two men waited, quietly watching the patrol as they continued to circle the building, it wasn’t until close to four hours later that they saw an opportunity. Nero had laid down and was lightly napping when Gilread nudged him with his foot. Nero was awake instantly “What is it” he said sitting up and wiping the sleep out of his eyes. “The patrol is going in, I think they are hunkering down for the night or changing soldiers, I am not sure” he said and Nero came up to look, peering out the slit in the wall he could see the horses entering the small village, laughter from the soldiers carried over the wind as they joked and talked amongst themselves to pass the time.

Once the soldiers were out of sight, Nero waited for another thirty minutes that seemed to go by slowly, each second an hour unto itself. Finally, he motioned for Gilread to follow and the two ran in a crouch down the hill. They quickly came to the edge of the village and using one of the few still standing sections they hid behind it for cover. Nero peered out from behind the wall to see the horses, without riders tied up to a post near a shop. The sign still half hanging off of the pole out front announced it to be the local BlackSmith.

He could see a small string of smoke coming from the half-collapsed chimney and a low light flickering as if it were flame. “They must be eathing” he whispered. Using the same low crouching run, they sprinted towards the keep halfway there the door to the smithy opened, Nero hit the ground flattening himself as Gilread did the same. Holding his breath, he watched as a soldier came out and surveyed the area, turning towards the side of the building he relieved himself with a content sigh. They two men lay stock still on the ground with the man not more then thirty feet from there location. If they were seen, they were dead Nero understood this as sweat broke out over his body.

The soldier finished his business and casually walked back into the building, laughter echoing out the door only to silence as it closed. The Messenger sighed, laying his head in the dirt and saying a short prayer. They both got up and finished rushing to the front of the old Keep.

The door was unlocked, and they went in and closed it behind them. Nero turned and did a doubletake, the keep was full, though not of people or things but supplies, boxes and bags of food and other sundries stacked from floor to ceiling stood in their way. Only a narrow aisle aloud any navigation to the front of the holy place. “What is this?” Gilread asked looking at the mountain of supplies that surrounded the two of them. “It’s the reason there are guards Gilread, this village is now a storehouse, though I am not sure why” he answered squeezing his way through the small space and coming to stand next to the podium. Since it had been carved from a solid piece of wood and extended into the foundation of the building it was next to impossible to move, so the soldiers had left the front area clear of boxes and bags.

“Help me Gilread” Nero said, as he tried to pry back a board behind the podium, the man looked at him curiosly and then crouched down to help. The board would not budge no matter how they pulled. “Give me a minute” Gilread said, moving back into the supplies and disappearing from sight. He returned a moment later with a smile and what looked like a flat piece of metal. “They left the pry bar” he said triumphiantly. Using the bar, they were able to peel back the boards giving them a four-foot opening. Peering into it Nero couldn’t see through the blackness in the hole and the two went searching again, this time finding one of the crystal lamps that had been thrown into a corner when they had cleaned out the old keep.

The glass was broken but after a moment of fiddling with the turn knob Nero was able to get a weak light and went over to the hold. Lowering the latern into it, he was rewarded with an ornate wooden lid of a coffin. Gilread looked confused “What?” he asked not understanding. Nero smiled “They didn’t put him in the ground, instead putting him under the floor should his sins come out and he need to be moved from this place. I never understood the decision, but sometimes those in charge don’t think through the concequences, I know for months the Messenger of the keep had to host services outside because of the smell, ever request to move the body was denied despite the pleas” Nero said grabbing the pry bar and putting it down into the hole. It took him a few attempts the area was tight and it didn’t give him a lot of leverage.

Finally, he was able to slide it between the lid and the cask, after a few pushes the lid popped. Pulling back the lid Nero shined the light into the coffin coming face to face with the mummified face of the old Lord Reagent dressed in his finest robes. Wincing he reached his hand into the coffin and began feeling around, it took nearly ten minutes before his hand closed over a velvet bag with something heavy inside. With a smile he slowly pulled up the bag and pulled out the heavy silver stamp that was the seal of the Lord Reagent. “Ive got it” he whispered, and he haphazardly replaced the boards.

Noticing the side room Nero made his way in to find the storage drawers used by the Messengers. Most of them were empty but in the final drawer he was rewarded with a few pages of old parchment and a small block of wax. He gently folded them and put them into his robes. Victorious, the two made their way back along the narrow space and had gone halfway through when Nero heard the door open. “Go back” he hissed to Gilread as the two began to shimmy back towards the pulpit. They disappeared around the edges of the mountain of supplies as Nero held his breath, the sound of slow booted footfalls echoing through the building. He heard the murmur of a voice from outside, but the one that answered was much closer. “I thought I heard something, give me a minute” the male voice shot back to whomever had spoken to him outside. Nero closed his eyes begging Aurtus to get away without being captured as the boots continued to move around the other side of the supplies.

He looked over to the other side of the small aisle and there was Gilread the man’s face was a mask of panic, Nero smiled at him making a calming gesture but ashis hand came down, the edge of his robe caught the prybar that had been laid on a supply box and it fell, hitting the floor with a loud thud. Both men winced and Nero heard the boots stop, standing still as the Soldier tried to narrow the location of the sound. After a moment he could hear the soldier moving again, but the pattern had changed and with dawning horror he realized the soldier was coming down the passage. “With a motion to Gilread he pushed himself up against the boxes trying to lessen the profile he would give off. Reaching into his pocked, his hand closed around the heavy seal and he pulled it out, raising it above his head he waited, listening as the sounds of shuffling came ever closer.

Then as he watched a hand appeared picking up the pry bar, holding it right in front of Nero the soldier grunted and as the two men listened the shuffling sound began to fade. After a few moments they listened as the boots crossed the open area and the door closed. Nero let out a breath that deflated his soul as he sagged with relief.

The two men shuffled through the supplies and stood waiting by the door as Nero fought his urge to open it and run. Slowly cracking it, he looked out and could see the light still in the smithy and he motioned Gilread, the two men exited the keep and ran as fast as they could to the barn. They reached it only a few minutes later, both men collapsing as their lungs burnt in their chest.

Once they had recovered, they made haste pushing the horses as fast as they could to make it back to the camp before dawn. Riding into the camp they were aloud back in by two disapproving guards after a lengthy explanation. Nero quickly made it back to the shack and sitting down scrawled a letter to the Lord Reagent of Turen, heating the wax he pressed the hard-won seal against the folded paper. “Is it done?” came Gilread’s voice from the door and Nero turned and smiled. “Yes, now we just need to get it there, Gilread, I need to find a messenger someone to take this letter and put it in the hands of the Lord Reagent of Turin, can you find me a volunteer, understand the future of Vicor may very well ride on the delivery of this letter” he said and the other man gave him a solemn nod leaving Nero to his thoughts.

An hour later a young lanky man stood in the small shack looking around nervously as Nero entered. “Master Gilread tells me you can ride young man, is this true?” he asked and the lanky man nodded “Yes Messenger, I ran the mail route between turen and a few of our smaller cities until… well until they closed the border Messenger” he answered and Nero smiled. “I need this letter delivered son, it is imperitave it gets to the Lord Regeant in Turen, do you undersand” he asked and the lanky man nodded, his eyes serious “I will make it so Messenger” he said and Nero reguarded him for a moment before nodding. “See Gilread, he will procure you a horse, once you have delivered the letter, wait for his response, and I hope his response includes troops” he said not daring to hope.

With the hopes of the camp and the future of there country on his shoulders the young man bolted forth riding the horse out and to the east for all he was worth. Nero entered his shack only to find an agitated Vira pacing the small floor, he was surprised to find her there “Vira, I know I should have told you of my trip but” he began but the woman cut him off. “That’s not it Nero, we have a problem, War is coming” she said and Nero nodded. He had been fielding that same worry from everyone. “I have just sent a message to Turen for assistance with troops to help us move somewhere out of the way, that doesn’t put us in the path of the enemy” he said smiling. But Vira did not share his smile instead the blonde capable women shot him a helpless look.

“No Nero, they are coming, now if we are here when they arrive, we will either be taken back as prisoners or slaughtered as examples” she said and nero’s stomach dropped about ten feet. “They are marching now. How do you know?” he demanded and Vira nodded “One of the Wardens who runs the patrol route south, brought us the news Nero, they will be here within a week” she finished. Walking over to his desk Nero slumped down into the chair “There is no way our support will be here in time, this came, all of the camps will be massacred” he whispered the vision of people swinging from poles as Ravens picked out their eyes flashed through his head.

“What do we do Vira, we can’t stay here” he said locking eyes with the woman who simply nodded but he could see the fear in her eyes as well. They were in the path of the Empresss war machine and they would not stop to worry about them, they would roll over this camp without even a thought. “We need to find someplace safe Nero, we need to get these people out of here, we cannot wait, these aren’t soldiers these are farmers who have lost everything not one is able bodied enough to stand against the forces bearing down on us” she stated. Nero knew this, understood this and yet finding a solution was buried under the self pity and doubt that swam through his mind. He was no general, no leader and yet now the fate of all of these people rested on his shoulders, how was he suppoed to save them when he couldn’t even save himself.

“Nero” Vira said, her voice even and firm, looking up he saw the resolve in her eyes, they were fierce and determined “We will find a way to save these people, but I need you to help” she said her eyes never leaving his. The fierce look of determination burning away his self doubt as his mind began to turn. “I need maps, Vira, can you find maps of the area” he asked bolting upright and the woman smiled, reaching into her pack and pulling out a stack of parchment “right here Messenger” she said smiling.

They spent the evening and well into the night pouring over the maps looking at every inch of every curve of ink that covered the old parchment hoping to divine some solution or some place they could glean from the information in front of them. But they were not scouting nor were they familiar with the areas shown. To them it was just lines and notes none of them giving a hint to a location that would squester his people from the oncoming storm. They gave up for the night agreeing to meet back the next day. Nero did not sleep that night instead lying awake as scene after scene of people dieing by the swords of the people who once protected them flashed through his mind.

In these scenes he failed to protect those who trusted him, those who put faith in his ability to keep them from harm. Finally, as the sun began to peak over the horizon, he mercifully left his bed, eyes bloodshot from his restless night he splashed water on his face and prepared a light breakfast. Vira did not show up until two hours later, by that time Nero had found himself pouring once again over the maps and seeing nothing that would help him. A knock came at the flimsy excuse for a door and looking up he found Vira an excited smile on her face as she led a grizzled looking man into the shack. “Messenger” the said nodding his head in deference, a religious man Nero thought nodding to him and turning to Vira. “Nero, we have it” she said excitedly, and he held his breath as she motioned for the woodsman to continue.

The man was filthy as if he had been working all night, his blonde hair was ratty with leaves and twigs haphazardly sticking out of it. His clothes were half covered with mud not all of it dry. “Who is this Vira?” Nero asked and the man stepped forward clearing his throat. “I am goric Messenger, a Master Warden” he simply said, and Nero nodded as a kernel of hope sprouted in his mind if anyone knew the area it would be the wardens he reflected, leaning back and motioning for the man to continue. Goric looked between the two of them shifting uncomfortably as he stood there for a moment trying to decide where to start. “Messenger, many years ago before the Wardens were given the keep, we housed ourselves in an old Lords villa to the west of here, about five days walk. I am not sure of the current state of the property, but with an army coming it will be out of the way and possibly defendable should the Empresss soldiers decide you are a worthy target” he said and then waited as Vira and Nero shot meaningful gazes at each other. “This is good information Goric, I thank you, Aurtus thanks you, you may have helped save these people, but I will need one more favor from you” Nero said gently and Goric nodded “What is it Messenger?” he asked.

A few hours later Goric had come through as a line of horses and a few carts of supplies lined up outside of the camps. Inside the four camps of Refugees it was pure chaos as everyone packed frantically. The Silvan’s though happy about the exodus of the Refugees, were not happy about the loss of supplies. Goric had convinced someone that for the low low price of the supplies their refugee problem would go away. It took almost four hours before everyone had mustered and lined up, the wounded were put in carts along with the old and the young. Vira’s female shooters took positions at the front and back of the caravan, at the very front rode Nero, Vira and Goric. Nero having requested the Warden as a guide to the location.

“Okay let’s get started” Nero said a smile on his face as for the first time in days, there was a real chance these people would be out of harms way. The caravan rode west slowly as the worn trade road was mostly unused and not easily traversed. The wagons shifted dangerously from side to side navigating water ruts forcing the group to keep to almost a walking pace. Nero had to keep himself calm and force down the frustration of the lack of progress five hours into the trip.

The caravan rode through the night Nero hearing a clock in his head, knowing the soldiers were on the way and needing to put distance between the border and his people tried his best to force more speed out of them, but to no avail. “So, I have to ask, what about the soldiers from Turen you requested” Vira asked on the third day as they continued to ride after an hour break for food. Nero smiled “I left them a note with the Silvan’s in case they showed up. Goric also left word with his people.” Nero finished, rubbing the ring that still felt new on his finger.

“What are we going to do when this is all over Nero, how are we going to rebuild. I image the Silvan’s; the Order and the Wardens are not going to stand by and allow the Empress her reign of terror” Vira proffered and Nero through about it for a moment. “There is something in place should we find outselves without a leader, it called the Royal Stuardship, a clause put into the Messengers that if needed the Church would steward the territory until a suitable ruler was found. It was added generations ago to ensure that should a ruler die without an heir; the country wouldn’t descend into bloodshed” he finished and Vira looked at him questioningly. “Why is it I have never heard of this?” she asked as if she were one who would know and Nero shot her a glance he had never asked the woman what she had done prior to being a refugee as he was considering how to do that he shrugged “It has never been enacted befores” he answered and Vira nodded. Nero continued to rub the ring that now weighed even more heavy upon his finger as he thought about the possibility of securing the country.

The rest of the journey was slow but uneventful and finally as they came around a corner on the old trade road a large grey stone wall rose in the distance. Goric smiled and pointed forward “Messenger, I give you Warden’s Hall” he said, and a cheer rose up from the line as the word spread, they were home. It took nearly a half of a day to finally reach the old wooden gate of the hall, Nero eyeing the rotten wood and the rusted hinges, the look of the wall was solid but everything else on it was either gone, rusted or broken which did not bode well for the rest of it he thought.

A small group went in first entering the overgrown courtyard as they surveyed the various buildings and the main hall, trees grew out of buildings and roofs had caved in long ago he noticed, but these things could be repaired and would give people something to do rather then wallow in fear of the Soldiers. He tasked Gilread to round up groups of able-bodied men and began the process of reparing a few of the surrounding buildings, they needed shelter and soon. Vira took charge of storing the carts within the wall as Goric himself went out to gather much needed wood to repair the door. Which left Nero wandering the complex, most of the people were cleaning up, chopping down or assisting in repairs.

Entering the large old hall swaths of sunlight lit the old worn stone floors as the roofs had caved in long ago, a tree now grew in the center of the cavernous hall reaching into the sky as a bed of rotten leaves covered the ground like carpet. He could see rotten abandoned pieces of what furniture at one time had been strewn about the area, but other then that the walls looked solid and the roof could be repaired. This would work he thought to himself, they could be safe here, weather the coming fight out of the way where the soldiers had no reason to go, he thought.

By the third day a few of the buildings had roofs and doors and people had begun to chip in more and more as they got settled Nero smiled as he watched repairs being done on all of the buildings left. The wall was solid and Goric had already begun to build a new solid door for the opening that was left when they removed the rotting wood that had once been the original protection for this place. As he strolled the compound nodding and offering words of encouragement, he could smell cooking meet from a tent setup at the rear where a line of people smiled and talked as they waited to eat. Things were going to be okay he thought looking around smiling “How are you today Messenger?” Vira’s voice came from behind him and Nero turned smiling and nodding at the woman. “Good, just inspecting the work and liking the progress, you know Vira for the first time in a while, I honestly believe we are going to be okay” he said smiling at her. She returned it nodding towards the wall. “My girls have been scouting out and tell me nothing at all is in our vicinity, we seem to be well out of the way here, so I think you might be right” she answered.

They lined up with the rest and ate lunch, talking about the work and the progress that had been made. After lunch Nero entered the main hall again, grabbing an axe he set his robe aside and began to remove the large tree in the center of the hall. Chop after chop he worked through the large trunk pieces of it flying as perspiration ran from his brow. It took him most of the day, ensuring the cut was true and that the angle would allow the tree to fall in the direction he wished, but by the time the sun fell to the trees there came a loud crack and the tree fell into the center of the large hall with a resounding crash. Nero smiled as he looked at the fruit of his labor, people crowded the door to see the downed tree. “Goric, do we have any woodsmiths with us, I believe I have found a new altar for the keep” he said, and a cheer rang out from the crowd and Nero laughed, something he had not done in many months he reflected.

But the haven was not as safe as he had thought, late that night as he slept soundly the dreams and visions of the villages he had seen and the atrocities he had been witness to faded a little, allowing him to sleep through the night an alarm went up through the camp and people scrambled out of bed and began to dress.

Nero burst out of the building that held forty people tightly until the rest of the facilities were completed and as he stepped into the open air a bone chilling shreak rose from the woods, a shreak he knew and one that sent a chill down his spine. “No, no Aurtus, not here” he whispered, looking around Nero did not know what to do, but thankfully Goric and Vira had appeared marshalling people to grab whatever they could find as a weapon they spread out over the courtyard as more of the shreaks rose from the woods, first three then five and then ten answered the original call. “It’s the demons, it’s the Lord Seers minions, they have found us” someone yelled from the courtyard, but Nero could not see them.

He looked around at the sixty people now scattered throughout the yard everyone’s head on a swivel as the screams echoed over the wall. The full moon gave them the ability to at least see, but see what he thought fighting the panic that began to well up inside. Then something ran along the wall, descending down again before he could get a look at it. It ran on all fours with the speed of a cat as it dashed. Screams echoed from somewhere near the back of the gate, not screams of fear no these were screams he had heard before, they were of pain and terror. Without so much as a thought for his own safety Nero dashed towards the sounds, people gathered as some tried to swing at whatever it was in the center of that crowd. But no sooner had a few tried then they were dragged down as well.

Nero burst through the crowd finding himself staring at the back wall and half open port gate as something hovered over a body its eyes glowed with blue hate as the creature hissed at the crowd. Then with the wave of its claw an unseen force hit the crowd driving them back as it focused back on its victim, Nero couldn’t tell who it was, the mask of torn meat and blood hit the unfortunate souls identity, but these things were mages he thought with horror.

They were too exposed, too out in the open, they needed to find someplace more secure he thought and then spotted the main hall, no it didn’t have a roof, but it did have walls. “Everyone, to the main hall” he screamed at them and then began shoving the shocked onlookers until they began to move.

How did they find them he wondered, why would they have been sent to kill them, they were nobodies, they had no military or strategic significance, the only thing they had done was to flee he thought? Then it dawned on him that the Empress might want to make an example of those who had escaped her, might want to show those still under her thumb that there was no hope. But in order to do that, they all would have to die. Nero pushed people harder, moving towards the keep as more shreeks rose from around them. Looking to his left he watched something rise up dragging down a poor girl who had found herself on the outside of the running crowd. To his right was another scream, but it quickly cut off and Nero didn’t want to think about the reason why.

The creatures were around them, picking off people as they desperately tried to make it to the main hall. A blast of fire hit to his left, igniting four people and killing them almost instantly. They were mages, or mage creations he thought. That same burning hatred he had developed since this had begun rekindled in force. This was the fault of those with the gift, those who the church had let live. This was the repayment for that mercy he thought hatred burning at his soul as he moved. More blasts of fire erupted around him as the creatures reigned down terror on the moving mob.

Then he was through the door, people pushing further back into the hall, trying to get away from the entrance as more screams erupted from behind. As the last of the survivors entered, Nero slammed the newly installed door, grabbing the bar and pushing it into place, he no sooner had done that when something slammed against the wood sending mortar spilling to the ground from around the frame.

Nero backed away from the entrance, watching it as something again slammed into it, sending more mortar to the floor.

Then a scream came from above and he looked up to see one of the creatures, perched on the edge of the torn and fallen roof. Before he could move it leaped from its perch, coming to land directly in front of Nero. He stared at the creature in horror, its corpse white skin and long limbs snaked out as it hissed at Nero, reaching for him. At that moment all sanity left the Messenger as the anger and hate that had been festering in his soul for months finally boiled over. With a loud scream Nero flung himself at the demon that now stood before them, wrapping his hands around its neck as they both fell to the ground. He slid his hands up the creatures face “No more, no more” he whispered over and over as his thumbs found its eyes and pushed with all his strength, he felt the small warm orbs resist the tips of his thumbs for only a moment before the warm black blood spilled around the socket and flowed to the floor from around his hands as he continued to push, harder and harder, feeling the bone at the back of the socket, he pushed even harder. The creature thrashed and bucked underneath him. He didn’t even feel the claws as they sliced through his robes and bit into his skin, wet blood pouring down onto the thing underneath him.

Wrapping his hands around its head, he began to pick it up and slam it back down over and over the creature mewling as it desperately tried to throw the Messenger off. Finally Nero heard a satisfying crack as the demon finally stopped moving, finally going still beneath him and he smiled a malevolent smile, they could be killed, they could be hurt he thought and tilted his head up to the sky, thrusting the black blooded fingers as if clawing at the moon and he screamed and screamed. As he did the creatures eight of them now perched above, slid away into the night.
